memory_update.text: MIDD should be retained as the reference public equipment platform for restaurant kitchen automation and QSR equipment replacement cycles, but not treated as the main underfollowed discovery candidate.
PAR is a priority underfollowed small-cap candidate for restaurant labor scheduling, back-office operations, inventory and data standardization exposure.

TACT is a speculative micro-cap shadow candidate with unusually direct back-of-house automation and food-safety workflow exposure; survival depends on evidence of material BOHA adoption and recurring revenue.
HBB is a below-USD-300M speculative exception for commercial beverage and compact food-prep equipment; later layers must verify whether commercial restaurant exposure is financially material.

Need a later pass on drive-thru voice AI, kitchen display systems, refrigeration/ice/beverage dispensing, warranty/service networks, NSF/UL/food-safety certification gates, and private suppliers that may map to public parents.

The node appears better framed as practical workflow and equipment modernization rather than humanoid robotics: ovens/fryers, back-office scheduling, food-safety labeling, temperature monitoring, beverage prep and service density are the immediate adoption surfaces.

node: Kitchen automation, beverage equipment, fry stations, ovens, drive-thru throughput, and labor-scheduling tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the restaurant labor-productivity/kitchen-automation node with a two-lane universe. The reference lane is Middleby, a public commercial-foodservice equipment platform with QSR exposure and automation-relevant ovens, fryers, warming, refrigeration, beverage and IoT assets. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller, less obvious public assets: PAR Technology for restaurant back-office scheduling/operations software, TransAct Technologies for BOHA back-of-house food-safety/task-labeling automation, and Hamilton Beach Brands as a below-USD-300M speculative exception tied to commercial beverage/food-prep equipment. Claims are intentionally kept at Layer 1 discovery level; later layers should verify customer concentration, restaurant-chain rollout evidence, recurring revenue attach rates, franchisee ROI, and whether exposure is large enough to matter financially.
